classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: No checks were run because the required data was not provided. The rule PSR-IN-R118 requires 'CTSH + VA 45%' (both tests must pass). To apply it, a bill of materials with each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency, plus a declaration with product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE and operations done in the UAE, are needed.

procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service. The factory must be located outside a free zone, have a MoIAT industrial licence and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Registration takes about 3 working days. Traders can apply only for goods bought from a registered factory.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice), and submit the application. Processing takes about one working day and the service runs 24/7.
Pay the certificate fee. The fee depends on the invoice value in AED and ranges from AED 10 to AED 200.

The certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from the date of issue and covers only one import (it may list several products). It should be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks) of India's certificate form.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue. Refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
